http://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/0.text: The captain of an oil tanker that collided with a cargo ship and sank off Istanbul leaving 10 crew missing has been arrested along with his third-in-command on charges of negligent homicide, prosecutors said on Friday.The pair were arrested by a court late on Thursday, a day after the pre-dawn collision in which the ALSU, an empty oil tanker, struck the Tuğberk İmamoğlu, a cargo vessel carrying rolled steel, in the Sea of Marmara near Istanbul.The case is being handled by prosecutors in Silivri on the western outskirts of Istanbul province.According to the prosecutors' statement, the Silvri court charged the pair with negligent homicide for failing to fulfil their navigational safety obligations and take the necessary measures to prevent the collision.It said the captain, identified only as A.E., "failed to fulfil his duty of supervision and oversight of navigational safety" while the other suspect, M.E., "who served as the third captain and watch officer at the time of the incident, failed to take the necessary measures to prevent the collision in a timely and effective manner."The court ordered four other suspects be granted conditional release, it said.Officials said the damaged cargo ship sank "very quickly" in waters about 900 metres deep, some 18 nautical miles (33 kilometres) off Silivri, leaving all 10 crew members missing.Rescuers have yet to reach the wreckage of the Tuğberk İmamoğlu or locate its voyage data recorder (VDR) or "black box."According to a marine accident expert report prepared for prosecutors, a copy of which was seen by the AFP news agency on Thursday, there were multiple breaches of safety procedures aboard the tanker."The fundamental root cause...resulting in a catastrophe, was the deficiencies and failures on the bridge of the M/T ALSU," it said.It said an inexperienced third officer was at the helm and there was no lookout on duty, describing it as "serious negligence.""No helmsman or lookout was posted on the bridge and the officer, who had only recently joined the vessel and lacked experience, was left alone on watch," the report said.It also pointed to shortcomings on the part of the cargo ship.Search and rescue operations continued on Friday.Prosecutors have started legal proceedings against nine of the ALSU's 10 crew members, excluding the cook, six of whom appeared in court on Thursday.

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/doctor-sh.text: Ethan Evans Updated Fri, August 28, 2026 at 2:59 PM UTC 0 Feeling hot and sweaty at night? -Credit:Getty Images Off the back of yet another heatwave, and as temperatures remain high , waking up hot and sweaty may seem like an unavoidable summer side effect. But there are times when it could be a cause for concern, and doctors have issued a reminder to pay attention to how often it happens as it can sometimes be linked to a deadly disease. Sweating is the body's natural way of cooling down, particularly when the mercury is soaring. Official NHS guidance says excessive sweating can happen even when the body does not need to cool down, and this could be linked to an underlying condition or medication. Drenching night sweats that repeatedly soak your clothes or bedding, especially when sleeping in a cool room, should not be dismissed, warns Dr Jidi Kubes. The radiation oncologist and medical director at Proton Therapy Center in Prague could be a sign you have cancer. Hidden switch that can turn off ageing found in body, universal flu vaccine made from yeast, Alzheimer's can spread like a virus, and an amazing bionic hand - all this and more in our science newsletter His warning comes as the death of country music legend Dolly Parton, aged 80, has put cancer back in the spotlight. Parton died in Nashville on August 25 following a brief battle with cancer, according to her publicist. • Dr Amir Khan explains exactly how much protein you need to eat every day to build muscle • Marcus Wareing opens up on 'most expensive meal in history' that cost £44,000 Dr Kubes said: “The important distinction is whether there is an obvious explanation. If the room is cool but you are repeatedly waking with your pyjamas and bedding soaked through, that is different from simply feeling clammy on a hot night.” The NHS says night sweats are when someone sweats so much that their nightclothes and bedding become soaking wet, even though their sleeping environment is cool. It advises speaking to a GP if they happen regularly, wake you up or cause concern. There are many possible explanations that have nothing to do with cancer. The NHS lists menopause, anxiety, some medicines, low blood sugar, alcohol and excessive sweating among potential causes, while infections can also trigger night sweats. However, Cancer Research UK says very heavy, drenching night sweats can be a general symptom of cancer and should be discussed with a doctor, particularly when there is no obvious explanation. Getting hot in bed -Credit:Getty Images/iStockphoto Night sweats are particularly associated with lymphoma, where they can occur alongside other so-called B symptoms. Cancer Research UK says these can include unexplained fevers and significant unintended weight loss, while painless swollen lymph nodes in the neck, armpit or groin are another common lymphoma symptom. Dr Kubes said people should seek medical advice sooner if severe sweating is accompanied by unexplained weight loss, persistent fatigue, recurring fevers or painless swelling. He stressed that cancer is “far from the most common explanation” for night sweats. The NHS also advises people with regular night sweats not to wait if they are worried, particularly if they also have a high temperature, cough, diarrhoea or unexplained weight loss. One or two sweaty nights during a heatwave are therefore unlikely to mean something serious on their own. But persistent, unexplained drenching sweats are worth raising with a GP, who can assess the symptom alongside any other changes in your health. Part of the reason why this allegation sounded plausible is that the spokesperson was unable to clearly show that this was something on the government’s agenda before the £72m story broke. (See 1.41pm.) https://www.jpost.com/international/inte.text: A Russian drone hit a passenger train on Ukraine's border with NATO member Poland on Sunday, shortly after former British prime minister Boris Johnson and other European diplomats had used the same line.The train, on a route frequently used by foreign delegations returning from Kyiv, was attacked just 2 kilometers from the Polish border, Ukraine's railway operator said.No casualties were reported.Johnson blamed Russian President Vladimir Putin in a statement after the attack. "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning," he wrote. I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning. What we can say for sure is that this is the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day - even on civilian railways. So far Putin…— Boris Johnson (@BorisJohnson) September 13, 2026"So far Putin has been responsible for the deaths of 1700 staff of Ukrzaliznytsia - Ukrainian Railways. They and their daily passengers are absolutely heroic. When are we going to give them the air defenses they need? Why won't we unfreeze Putin's cash and give it to Ukraine?""We will get this dreadful war over much faster if we all get serious and give them what they need and deserve," he finished. "This wasn't our train, but the one just minutes after us by the border crossing. It was evacuated as the drone approached and no one was hurt," Carl Bildt, former Swedish prime minister, said on X/Twitter.Bildt, Boris Johnson, and other European politicians were returning to Poland by train after attending a security conference in Kyiv when they were awoken at 5 a.m. and prepared to evacuate.Russia's strike may have been targeting the diplomats' train"It is entirely possible that the Russian drone's intended target was the diplomatic train, which departed the station earlier than scheduled after train timetables were adjusted in real time because of the constant threat of Russian strikes," Ukraine's railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said on Telegram.Johnson left the station shortly before the strike and condemned the attack as "random and senseless" in a post on Instagram.With the front line largely static, both Moscow and Kyiv have intensified long-distance strikes in recent weeks to try to shift momentum in the war.Polish foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski described Russia's increasing attacks on NATO's doorstep as "an escalation."Earlier on Sunday, a truck less than 1 km. from Ukraine's border with Poland was also hit, prompting the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing point to briefly halt operations, according to border guards.Russia's Defense Ministry said it had targeted infrastructure facilitating military cargoes from Europe in Western Ukraine.Russia has begun targeting Ukraine's border crossings with its Western allies in recent weeks, part of a growing campaign by both sides to erode the other's economic infrastructure more than four years into Russia's invasion.Johnson joined the conference as an adviserThe former prime minister of the UK was in Ukraine alongside advisors from several other European nations for the 2026 annual meeting of the Yalta European Strategy, a defense conference where specialists discussed potential ceasefire negotiations with Russia with Volodymyr Zelensky's government.“ These drone attacks are blind terror against Ukrainian civilians and a dangerous escalation in Putin's war," said Robin Wagener, a Green Party member of the German Parliament, who was also on board the train.The Polish Air Force mobilized after the strikes occurred within two kilometers of Polish territory, a NATO member. “Due to the activity of the Russian Federation's jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory, military aviation operations have commenced in Polish airspace,” Polish military personnel said in a statement to social media.Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the attacks afterward.“It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every day, give their lives, and do not allow the aggression to expand.”

Photograph: Brandon Bell/Getty Images Austin Man arrested over alleged plot to attack Texas state capitol Suspect Benny Caldera Jr held on bond as officials say they received ‘credible’ information about Austin threat Uwa Ede-Osifo and agency Wed 30 Sep 2026 21.28 EDT First published on Wed 30 Sep 2026 19.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 40-year-old man was arrested early Wednesday on suspicion of plotting to attack the Texas state capitol, authorities said. The Texas department of public safety said in a statement that it received “credible information about an individual planning a violent attack” for Thursday in Austin . Benny Caldera Jr told a friend, “I am going to the Capitol and I am going to shoot it up,” according to an arrest warrant affidavit obtained by NBC 5 DFW. “I love you, if you don’t see me again,” Caldera allegedly told the friend, police wrote in the arrest documents. Caldera had expressed anger over the American Israeli Public Affairs Committee (Aipac), NBC 5 DFW reported. “These people have to be exterminated,” Caldera allegedly said. The tip came in Tuesday evening, and Swat officers arrested Caldera at about 3am on Wednesday at a residence in Converse, Texas, near San Antonio. Caldera has been charged with felony terroristic threat against a public servant, court records show. He has been released after posting a $75,000 bond. Messages were left seeking comment from an attorney listed for Caldera. Public safety officials notified state lawmakers about the threat and arrest early on Wednesday. The Capitol remained open during regular operating hours. Texas senate secretary Patsy Spaw said in a notice that there will be increased security at the Capitol during the investigation. Governor Greg Abbott said the state DPS was assisted by the FBI in making the arrest. “Texas will NOT tolerate threats of violence against our Capitol,” the governor said in a statement on social media.
